canvas-editor.cell: no server route: it measures and paints on a browser canvas
canvas-editor.why: canvas-editor measures every character with a canvas 2D context and paints each page on a `<canvas>` it creates in the DOM. The package has no headless entry, so running it here would mean faking a browser.

cite-check.cell: no server route: it is canvas-editor with an application on top
cite-check.why: cite-check is an application built on canvas-editor, and draws through it: the same reason as canvas-editor.

apryse.cell: no server route: Apryse renders on a server with a native SDK
apryse.why: WebViewer is Apryse's browser product. Its server rendering is a native SDK and a Docker service (WebViewer Server); a Val runs neither native binaries nor subprocesses.

nutrient.cell: no server route: Nutrient renders on a server with a Docker service
nutrient.why: The Web SDK converts the .docx in the browser with a .NET engine in WebAssembly that it fetches from its own workers. Nutrient's server rendering is Document Engine, a Docker service; a Val runs neither native binaries nor subprocesses.

react-docx.cell: no server route: it breaks pages by measuring text in the browser
react-docx.why: `@extend-ai/react-docx@0.15.0` exports browser entries only (`.`, `./vanilla`, `./internal`). Its Rust parser in WebAssembly needs no DOM, but pagination measures text with a canvas `measureText` and with laid-out elements (`getBoundingClientRect`), and its page-image renderer throws "DOCX thumbnails require a browser environment". A route could send the parsed text, but the page breaks would be ours, not its.

univer.cell: no server route: no .docx reader, and its layout measures text on a canvas
univer.why: Univer's open-source packages cannot read a .docx (import and export are in its separately licensed Server SDK), so even in the browser this site hands it text and headings. Its layout (`@univerjs/engine-render@1.5.2`) takes text measurements from a canvas 2D context and has none without `document` or `OffscreenCanvas`.

onlyoffice.cell: no server route: its converter is built without the renderer, and drawing needs the editor in a browser
onlyoffice.why: CryptPad compiles x2t to WebAssembly with OnlyOffice's `doctrenderer` replaced by an empty stub, so it converts between formats but cannot lay out or draw: x2t sends PDF and HTML output through that renderer. Pages are drawn by the editor's JavaScript (sdkjs) on a browser canvas. OnlyOffice's own server rendering is the native Document Server or Document Builder, which a Val cannot run.
